newsitem.title: UK: UK retail prices rise yr/yr 2.4 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: UK retail prices rise yr/yr 2.4 pct in April.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics released the following April retail price indices.
RETAIL PRICES INDEX APRIL MARCH APR 96
Mth pct change ex MIPs, tax 0.3 0.3 0.7
COMPONENT DETAILS OF THE ALL-ITEMS INDEX (PCT CHANGES) -
NOTE - Consensus forecast was RPI +0.6 pct month-on-month and +2.5 pct YY, RPIX +2.6 pct YY, RPIY +2.2 pct YY.

The RPI all-goods measure rose 1.7 percent year on year in April, down from 2.0 percent in the year to March. The all-services RPI rose 3.3 percent in the year to April, unchanged from the March rate.

The ONS said the fall in the all-items 12-month rate was largely due to motoring costs, where prices for vehicles and petrol and oil dropped over the month. Housing costs, household goods and leisure goods prices also had downward effects.
Upward pressures on the 12-month rate came from seasonal food prices and charges for household services.
The ONS said the seasonal fall in vegetable prices was less steep than last April following the unusually sharp reductions of recent months. Fresh fruit and potato prices also had an upward effect.
There was downward pressure from home killed lamb prices as April's seasonal rise was smaller than the rise seen last year which followed a government announcement about BSE.
In non-seasonal food, upward pressure on the 12-month rate came from price rises for coffee and processed vegetables and fewer offers on beef and fresh milk prices than last year.
* RPIX lowest since Nov 1994 when rate was 2.3%.
